mechanism: 锁定同一成年人物、正面步行轴和同一商业街结构，让夏、秋、冬、春依次同步改写树木、地面、光线和服装；人物的脸、发型、杯子与步态连续，终局回到明亮季节并靠近镜头。 The reusable mechanism preserves causal order, spatial anchors and the final proof while replacing every source-specific person, location, object, wording, choreography and design.

invariants.rule: One clearly adult identity, one frontal walking axis, one carried cup and fixed street geometry persist through all states.
invariants.purpose: Establishes the baseline identity, object or geography that every later state must preserve.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact baseline rule, later changes cannot be attributed to the same subject, object or place, so the sequence loses its reference state. Removed rule: "One clearly adult identity, one frontal walking axis, one carried cup and fixed street geometry persist through all states."

invariants.rule: Every seasonal transition simultaneously updates foliage, ground, light and declared wardrobe.
invariants.purpose: Makes the visible trigger precede and explain the first mechanism response.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact trigger rule, the response appears spontaneously and the central cause-and-effect claim is no longer demonstrated. Removed rule: "Every seasonal transition simultaneously updates foliage, ground, light and declared wardrobe."

invariants.rule: Face, hairstyle, glasses, cup, stride and body proportions cannot change with the environment.
invariants.purpose: Keeps the middle progression registered instead of allowing an unexplained reset.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact progression rule, the middle can jump to a replacement state and the accumulated result is no longer traceable. Removed rule: "Face, hairstyle, glasses, cup, stride and body proportions cannot change with the environment."

invariants.rule: Foreground transition carriers occur once per season and reveal registered storefronts rather than new geography.
invariants.purpose: Reconnects the changed or partial state to the established subject and spatial anchor.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact reconnection rule, detail or transformed shots can belong to a different subject or geography and continuity cannot be verified. Removed rule: "Foreground transition carriers occur once per season and reveal registered storefronts rather than new geography."

invariants.rule: The terminal closer view retains the same adult and cup in the final season under one exact original title.
invariants.purpose: Turns the terminal hold into observable proof that the mechanism completed.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact terminal-proof rule, the sequence stops on motion alone and never confirms the promised outcome or preserved aftermath. Removed rule: "The terminal closer view retains the same adult and cup in the final season under one exact original title."

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: all source faces, bodies, wardrobe, identities and creator-specific character designs
the source location, set dressing, props, products and exact environmental geometry
all source words, logos, watermarks, typefaces and brand identifiers
the source choreography, exact camera path, shot durations and transition timing
the source palette, signature effects, prompt wording, creator handle and narrative particulars
